quests.instruction: Which storage space is built right into the wall of a bedroom, with its own door?
quests.question: Closet
quests.hint: This storage space is part of the room itself, not a separate piece of furniture.
quests.explanation: That's right! A closet is a storage space built right into the wall of a room.
quests.funFact: Many closets have a long bar inside just for hanging shirts and jackets.

quests.instruction: Which outdoor space is an open, grassy area around a home, perfect for playing games?
quests.question: Yard
quests.hint: This space is mostly open grass, without rows of planted flowers.
quests.explanation: Yes! A yard is an open, grassy space around a home, great for playing outside.
quests.funFact: Many families set up a swing set or play catch out in their yard.

quests.instruction: Which barrier is built outdoors to mark the edge of a yard?
quests.question: Fence
quests.hint: This barrier stands outside, often made of wood or metal, around a yard.
quests.explanation: That's right! A fence is an outdoor barrier that marks the edge of a yard.
quests.funFact: A fence around a yard helps keep a family dog safely inside.

quests.instruction: Which object would you turn with your hand to actually open the door?
quests.question: Doorknob
quests.hint: You twist this round or lever-shaped object to open a door.
quests.explanation: Yes! A doorknob is the round handle you twist with your hand to open a door.
quests.funFact: Some doorknobs have a lock built right into the middle.

quests.instruction: Which barrier stands inside a home, dividing one room from another?
quests.question: Wall
quests.hint: This barrier is indoors, holding up the roof and separating rooms.
quests.explanation: Yes! A wall stands inside a home, dividing rooms and holding up the roof.
quests.funFact: Many families hang pictures and photographs on the walls of their home.

quests.instruction: Which entrance would you open to walk directly into a house?
quests.question: Door
quests.hint: This entrance is part of the house itself, with hinges and a knob.
quests.explanation: That's right! A door is the entrance you open to walk directly into a house.
quests.funFact: Knocking on a door is a polite way to ask before walking inside.

quests.instruction: Old photo albums are stored at the very top of the house, right under the roof. Which room is this?
quests.question: Attic
quests.hint: Climb up, not down, to reach this storage space.
quests.explanation: That's right! An attic sits at the very top of a house, right under the roof.
quests.funFact: Some attics have a small window that lets in a little bit of daylight.

quests.instruction: Which entrance would you open to walk into a fenced yard?
quests.question: Gate
quests.hint: This entrance is built into a fence, not into the house itself.
quests.explanation: Yes! A gate is the entrance built into a fence, leading into a yard.
quests.funFact: Closing a gate behind you helps keep a family pet safely inside the yard.

quests.instruction: Which object would a visitor press to let you know they have arrived?
quests.question: Doorbell
quests.hint: Pressing this object makes a ring or a chime sound.
quests.explanation: That's right! A doorbell is pressed by a visitor to make a ring or chime sound.
quests.funFact: Some doorbells even show a live video of whoever is standing outside.

quests.instruction: Old furniture is stored below the ground floor, underneath the rest of the house. Which room is this?
quests.question: Basement
quests.hint: Go down, not up, to reach this storage space.
quests.explanation: Yes! A basement sits below the ground floor, often partly underground.
quests.funFact: Basements often stay nice and cool, even on a hot summer day.

quests.instruction: Which kitchen appliance has burners on top for frying eggs or boiling soup in a pot?
quests.question: Stove
quests.hint: Pots and pans sit right on top of this appliance.
quests.explanation: That's right! A stove has burners on top for frying, boiling, and simmering food.
quests.funFact: Some stoves use gas flames, while others use electric heat to warm a pan.

quests.instruction: Which kitchen appliance is an enclosed box used to bake cookies or a birthday cake?
quests.question: Oven
quests.hint: You place food inside and close the door for this one.
quests.explanation: Yes! An oven is an enclosed box that bakes food evenly all around, like cookies and cakes.
quests.funFact: An oven can get extremely hot, so it is always opened carefully with oven mitts.

quests.instruction: Dad wants his own comfy seat with armrests, just big enough for one person to relax alone. Which piece of furniture is this?
quests.question: Armchair
quests.hint: This chair has two armrests and is made for only one person at a time.
quests.explanation: Yes! An armchair is a cozy seat built for just one person, unlike a sofa that fits several.
quests.funFact: Many armchairs come with a matching footstool so you can rest your feet too.

quests.instruction: Which bathroom fixture fills up with water so you can sit down and soak?
quests.question: Bathtub
quests.hint: You sit inside this and let it fill with warm water.
quests.explanation: That's right! A bathtub fills with water so you can sit and soak, unlike a shower where you stand.
quests.funFact: Some bathtubs have bubbles or rubber ducks to make bath time extra fun.

quests.instruction: Which piece of furniture stands on its own, with doors, for hanging clothes?
quests.question: Wardrobe
quests.hint: This is a standalone piece of furniture, not a space built into the wall.
quests.explanation: Yes! A wardrobe is a standalone piece of furniture with doors for hanging clothes.
quests.funFact: Long ago, before closets were built into walls, every home needed a wardrobe.

quests.instruction: Three family members want to sit together and watch a movie. Which piece of furniture seats them all side by side, unlike a chair made for just one person?
quests.question: Sofa
quests.hint: This piece of furniture is long enough for more than one person to sit on.
quests.explanation: That's right! A sofa is long enough to seat several people together, while an armchair only fits one.
quests.funFact: A sofa is sometimes called a couch, but both words mean the exact same piece of furniture.

quests.instruction: Which bathroom fixture sprays water down from above so you rinse off while standing up?
quests.question: Shower
quests.hint: Water falls down on you from above while you stand underneath.
quests.explanation: Yes! A shower sprays water from above while you stand, using less water than a full bathtub.
quests.funFact: Taking a shower instead of a bath often saves a lot of water.

quests.instruction: Which part of a home is a flat passage that connects different rooms on the same floor?
quests.question: Hallway
quests.hint: You walk straight along this passage, without stepping up or down.
quests.explanation: That's right! A hallway is a flat passage that connects rooms on the same floor.
quests.funFact: Some hallways have closets along the wall for storing coats and shoes.

quests.instruction: Which outdoor space is filled with planted flowers and vegetables that need watering to grow?
quests.question: Garden
quests.hint: This space is planted with flowers or vegetables, not just plain grass.
quests.explanation: That's right! A garden is planted with flowers or vegetables that need care to grow.
quests.funFact: Bees and butterflies love visiting the colorful flowers growing in a garden.

quests.instruction: Which part of a home has steps that lead from one floor up to another?
quests.question: Stairs
quests.hint: You step up or down along this part of a home, instead of walking flat.
quests.explanation: Yes! Stairs are a row of steps that connect one floor of a home to another.
quests.funFact: Many stairs have a railing on the side to help you hold on safely.

quests.instruction: Which entrance has a knob or handle you turn to enter a room?
quests.question: Door
quests.hint: This flat, hinged panel leads between rooms or into the house.
quests.explanation: Correct! A door has a knob or handle you turn to enter a room or house.
quests.funFact: Most doors swing open on small metal hinges attached to one side.

quests.instruction: If you wanted to relax by soaking in warm water up to your shoulders, which fixture would you use?
quests.question: Bathtub
quests.hint: This fixture holds still water around your whole body while you sit.
quests.explanation: Correct! A bathtub holds still water so you can soak your whole body while sitting.
quests.funFact: Many young children enjoy playing with toys while sitting in the bathtub.

quests.instruction: Which piece of furniture could be moved to a different room if a family wanted to rearrange?
quests.question: Wardrobe
quests.hint: This piece of furniture can be pushed or carried, unlike a space built into a wall.
quests.explanation: That's right! A wardrobe is a movable piece of furniture, unlike a built-in closet.
quests.funFact: Some wardrobes also have drawers at the bottom for folded clothes.

quests.instruction: Which storage space might have shoes, coats, and a few boxes tucked inside?
quests.question: Closet
quests.hint: This space is a small area built into the wall, with a door of its own.
quests.explanation: Correct! A closet is a small storage space built into the wall, perfect for shoes and coats.
quests.funFact: Tidying your closet regularly makes it much easier to find your favorite outfit.

quests.instruction: Which part of a home would you climb to reach a bedroom on a higher floor?
quests.question: Stairs
quests.hint: Each step here is a little higher than the one before it.
quests.explanation: That's right! Stairs are steps you climb to reach a room on a higher floor.
quests.funFact: Climbing stairs is actually a great way to get some healthy exercise.

quests.instruction: Which outdoor space would a family mow to keep the grass short and neat?
quests.question: Yard
quests.hint: This open, grassy space usually needs regular mowing, not watering flower beds.
quests.explanation: That's right! A yard is the open, grassy space that families mow to keep it neat.
quests.funFact: A big yard gives kids plenty of room to run, play, and kick a ball.

quests.instruction: Which appliance would you use to bake a tray of cookies until they turn golden brown?
quests.question: Oven
quests.hint: This appliance has a door you open and close, with heat inside.
quests.explanation: That's right! An oven bakes food like cookies inside its enclosed, heated space.
quests.funFact: Many families love the warm, sweet smell that fills the kitchen while cookies bake.

quests.instruction: Which piece of furniture usually faces the television so the whole family can watch shows together?
quests.question: Sofa
quests.hint: More than one person can sit on this long, cushioned seat at the same time.
quests.explanation: Correct! A sofa is long and soft, giving the whole family room to sit together.
quests.funFact: Sofas are often decorated with extra cushions to make them even comfier.

quests.instruction: Which room is often partly underground and stays cooler than the rest of the house?
quests.question: Basement
quests.hint: This storage space is the lowest room, often below ground level.
quests.explanation: That's right! A basement is often built partly underground, keeping it cool.
quests.funFact: Some basements are turned into a cozy extra playroom or movie room.

quests.instruction: Which part of a home would you walk along, without stepping up or down, to reach your bedroom?
quests.question: Hallway
quests.hint: This passage stays flat the whole way, connecting nearby rooms.
quests.explanation: Correct! A hallway stays flat and connects nearby rooms on the very same floor.
quests.funFact: Long hallways are a fun place for kids to walk in a nice straight line.
